mechanism_narrative: The continued week-over-week easing in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES implies more commuting and in-person activity is stabilizing, which should lift retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remaining at or above their current levels.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and WORKPLACES stays below baseline, more discretionary shopping shifts to local retail trips outside commuting hours, pushing RETAIL_REC upward within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 5% while WORKPLACES remains below 0%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls or stays below its last 4-week mean after RESIDENTIAL remains above 5% and WORKPLACES remains below 0% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in TRANSIT indicates fewer trips into dense commercial areas, and retail-and-recreation mobility will decline over the next month if transit usage crosses a negative threshold from the current level.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days after TRANSIT falls below -5% and stays there for at least two weekly observations.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent weakness in PARKS usually reflects weather or seasonal outdoor substitution that also suppresses shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC will drift lower over the next four weeks when PARKS remains depressed.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above its last 4-week mean while PARKS stays below -15% for the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM stays strongly elevated while PARKS remains weak, households are concentrating trips on essentials and not on discretionary outings, which should keep retail and recreation below its recent average over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean while GROCERY_PHARM remains above 35% and PARKS remains below -15% for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in RETAIL_REC is mechanically supported by recovery in WORKPLACES because the same daily-trip network expands lunch, errand, and after-work shopping opportunities over the next week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within the next week after WORKPLACES posts two consecutive weekly gains.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, simultaneous gains in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are a stronger signal of resumed downtown access than either series alone, and that joint recovery should raise retail and recreation mobility over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both cross above their prior 4-week means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains at or below its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES move above their prior 4-week means.

mechanism_narrative: The current pattern of high GROCERY_PHARM and muted PARKS suggests errands are substituting for leisure trips; if that substitution persists, discretionary retail visits will be lower over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above its last 4-week mean while GROCERY_PHARM stays above 35% and PARKS stays below -20% for most of the next 28 days.
